resources.string: Dial in international format when roaming
Turning this off leaves calls exactly as if Roamer were not installed.
Only used by the setting above, for when the network country cannot be detected.
"system-prefixed" means Android supplied the prefix and Roamer passed the call through, which is the normal case.

Android already works out the full international number using the country you are in — but it does not dial that form unless an app asks it to.\n\nRoamer is that app: it hands the international number back to Android so it is the one actually dialled. That is all it does for almost every call.
Use local SIM for local calls
On a dual-SIM phone, place calls to the country you are in through that country\'s SIM. Needs phone permission.

Off by default. Android normally works out the country prefix itself. This only affects numbers it could not recognise — and because a local number gives no clue which country it belongs to, Roamer has to guess the country you are in. A home number typed without its prefix would then be dialled in the wrong country.
